Cells, each printing its symbol stacked over its name: reject × H1 = 'Power' over '(1 – β)' [BLUE-SHADED]; reject × H0 = 'α' over 'Type I error'; not-reject × H1 = 'β' over 'Type II error'; not-reject × H0 = EMPTY of text [BLUE-SHADED]. The legend 'Blue shading = correct result.' prints below the grid's bottom-left edge. The grid's labels extract INTERLEAVED in the raw text layer (Reality / Study rejects H0 / Study does not reject H0 / H1 / H0 / Power / α / ( 1 – β) / Type I error / β / Type II error / Blue shading = correct result.) — the cell assignment pinned by bbox + the two VLM passes; the first full-page pass mis-read the column headers and was overruled (see adjudication).

inventory.visualPurpose: The Statistical vs clinical significance block (book 266): the two definitions side by side — statistical significance defined by the likelihood of results being due to chance vs clinical significance as a measure of effect on treatment outcomes — sealed by the printed 1 mg/dL blood-sugar example of high statistical significance with limited clinical impact
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: TEXT BLOCK WITH LABEL COLUMN, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM-read at 120dpi, staging-pubh14/vlm-census.txt): the block title 'Statistical vs clinical significance' wraps across two lines in its left label column (a documented quirk); the body prints three sentences at the right: 'Statistical significance—defined by the likelihood of study results being due to chance. If there is a high statistical significance, then there is a low probability that the results are due to chance.' (lead-in in blue); 'Clinical significance—measure of effect on treatment outcomes. An intervention with high clinical significance is likely to have a large impact on patient outcomes/measures.' (lead-in in blue); and the example sentence 'Some studies have a very high statistical significance, but the proposed intervention may have limited clinical impact/significance, eg, a study might show a statistical significance of lowered blood sugar levels by 1 mg/dL correlated with better outcomes, but this may not be clinically as important.' The indd footer slug extracts between the title and the body in the raw layer (reading-order artifact; it prints at the page foot).
inventory.kypLocation: Zone D of the registry visual (HypothesisErrorsMap in visuals/pubhealth-p14.tsx): the two definitions as side-by-side half-cards (statistical significance — the chance language; clinical significance — the patients language) over the printed-example strip carrying the 1 mg/dL blood-sugar sentence verbatim; the block's text is ALSO carried verbatim in the note's core.what, the clinical block, usmle.patterns[3], and recall[8]
